images.caption: Figure 2:The general workflow and components of our framework.

Figure 3:Left: The query-view-centric selection module. Middle: The coarse ray-surface distance regressor, which seamlessly integrates pointmap- and ray-based representations. Right: The raylet-based surface module, which further refines the initially estimated surfaces.
Figure 4:Qualitative results of our method and baselines for ray distance on novel views.
Figure 5:Qualitative results of our method and baselines for normal estimation on novel views.
Figure 6:Qualitative results of normal derivation on novel views by different techniques.
Figure 7:Qualitative results of our method and baselines for 3D surface reconstruction under different input views.
Figure 8:Qualitative results of our method and baselines for 3D surface reconstruction on multiple datasets.
Figure 9:Qualitative results of our method and baselines for single view 3D surface reconstruction on Replica.
Figure 10:Qualitative comparison of surfel-based reference selection.
Figure 11:Details of U-Net feature extractor. Block means a sequential application of SparseConvolution in encoder or SparseInverseConvolution in decoder, GroupNorm and ReLU activation.
Figure 12:Qualitative 3D results of our method and baselines on ScanNet++. The upper two rows compare 3D meshes, and the bottom two rows compare 3D point clouds.
Figure 13:Failure cases of our method. For example, the mirror and transparent glasses on the wall cause inaccurate pointmap estimation by VGGT, which ultimately leads to errors in our approach.
